CHECKLIST 05
Hell Terrain Finalisation
LOCKED IMPLEMENTATION SPECIFICATION v1.0

rows:
STATUS
COMPLETE / LOCKED at implementation-design level. This document closes CHECKLIST 05. Exact Warden teams remain owned by CHECKLIST 04 and are reproduced here only as frozen dependencies. Runtime battle testing remains a validation gate: any later mechanical change requires an explicit Checklist 05 revision rather than silent tuning.

blocks.text: Canonical creature terminology: Abyssal / Abyssals. Legacy source filenames may still contain older project wording.

rows:
LOCK SUMMARY
Eight persistent Warden native fields are fixed. All field effects are symmetric and readable. Gilded Dust includes the Rock Special Defence boost; Cocytus Hail includes the Ice Defence boost. Standard field/weather moves or abilities may temporarily replace a native Warden field, after which the native field automatically resumes.

blocks.text: 1. Canon authority and completion boundary
• Use the locked story sequence, Warden identities, Circle order and themes as fixed narrative canon.
• Use CHECKLIST 04 as the sole authority for each Warden’s six-Abyssal roster, levels, held-role allocations, deterministic abilities, legal-move resolution and Warden AI tier.
• CHECKLIST 05 owns the exact native field modifiers, persistence, replacement/resumption rules, HUD/readability requirements and terrain-specific counterplay.
• Warden difficulty must come from the visible field plus the frozen team and AI. There are no hidden Warden-only stat multipliers, secret accuracy penalties or input-reading effects.
• Every native field rule applies equally to both sides whenever its condition is met. A player Abyssal receives the same type modifier, immunity or defensive field bonus as an enemy Abyssal.
• Boss-specific story presentation may sit beside a native field, but it may not silently add extra terrain mechanics.

rows:
IMPLEMENTATION PRINCIPLE
Warden fields are normal readable battle fields with roughly Sun/Rain/Sand/Hail complexity. Their purpose is to distort familiar matchup assumptions without turning any fight into a separate minigame or hiding core battle information.

blocks.text: 2. Global Warden-field contract
• Native field timing: the Warden’s field is active before Turn 1. The battle intro must announce it before the player selects the first command.
• Native duration: indefinite for the Warden battle. It has no natural turn countdown and is not tied to a particular enemy party slot.

• No stacking: only one active field/weather ruleset applies at a time. A temporary replacement completely suspends the native Warden field; it does not sit underneath and continue applying bonuses or chip.
• Temporary replacement: any otherwise-legal field/weather-setting move or ability may replace the active native Warden field according to that move/ability’s normal duration or rule.
• Automatic resumption: when a temporary replacement expires or is cleared, the native Warden field returns immediately and indefinitely. It does not need to be recast by the Warden.

• No permanent dispel: a move that only clears weather cannot create a permanent neutral battlefield. Clearing a temporary replacement causes the native Warden field to reassert; attempting to clear the native field itself leaves it active.
• Replacement chaining: a new temporary field replaces the previous temporary field by normal battle rules. When the final temporary field ends, the native Warden field resumes.
• Battle-end priority: once the Warden’s final Abyssal is defeated and the battle has resolved as won, no additional native-field chip tick is processed purely after victory.
3. Locked field quick reference

blocks.text: 4. Veyr, Keeper of Names — Namefog

rows: Trucepoe Lv105; Reversire Lv106; Idolure Lv107; Sigilume Lv108; Sepulshade Lv109; Pandemne Lv110
Slots 3 and 6 use Hidden Abilities; all other slots follow the frozen Checklist 04 authored assignments.
Break certainty, obscure identity and punish rote targeting without hiding the actual battle interface.

blocks.text: Field contract
• All Ghost-type damaging moves deal ×1.5 damage.
• All Psychic-type damaging moves deal ×0.5 damage.
• Namefog does not alter accuracy, evasion, command labels, party information, target selection or move names.
• Type immunities remain absolute. A Ghost move into a normal immunity still deals 0 damage before the field multiplier matters.
Viable counterplay
• Normal-type immunity can blank boosted Ghost damage where the normal type chart grants that immunity.
• Dark pressure and strong neutral coverage avoid dependence on the suppressed Psychic channel.
• A legal temporary field replacement turns Namefog off for its duration.
5. Ossael, the Gatherer — Gilded Dust

rows: Ampullusk Lv115; Bastimole Lv116; Ibracle Lv117; Trebuchor Lv118; Cyprigon Lv119; Mausolisk Lv120
Slots 3 and 6 use Hidden Abilities; all other slots follow the frozen Checklist 04 authored assignments.
Sand/hoard pressure: slow denial, recovery and defensive switching into a heavy ace.

blocks.text: Field contract
• At the normal end-of-turn field-damage step, every non-Rock/Ground/Steel active Abyssal loses 1/16 of maximum HP.
• Rock, Ground and Steel Abyssals are immune to Gilded Dust chip damage.
• While Gilded Dust is active, Rock Abyssals receive a ×1.5 Special Defence effective-stat modifier.
• The ×1.5 Rock Special Defence modifier is a field modifier, not a visible stat stage. It applies to either side and disappears immediately while Gilded Dust is suppressed.
• Ground and Steel receive chip immunity only; they do not receive the Rock Special Defence bonus unless their actual typing also includes Rock.
Viable counterplay
• Rock/Ground/Steel party members ignore the chip component; player Rock types also gain the Special Defence bonus.
• Pressure the frozen roster through its actual weaknesses rather than trying to race chip with fragile neutral units.
• Recovery, protection and a legal temporary field replacement are valid answers; replacing Gilded Dust suspends both chip and the Rock Special Defence bonus.
6. Mordren, Drum of War — Blood Sun

rows: Sunscint Lv127; Cehong Lv128; Liontide Lv129; Oriflamme Lv130; Regnacra Lv131; Gehennuar Lv132
Slots 3 and 6 use Hidden Abilities; all other slots follow the frozen Checklist 04 authored assignments.
Sun-style aggression with mixed Fire and non-Fire beneficiaries.

blocks.text: Field contract
• All Fire-type damaging moves deal ×1.5 damage.
• All Water-type damaging moves deal ×0.5 damage.
• Blood Sun does not automatically add unrelated later-generation Sun side effects. Move-specific effects continue to follow the move catalogue.
• The modifier is symmetric: player Fire is also boosted and player Water is also suppressed.
Viable counterplay
• Ground, Rock and strong neutral attacks avoid relying on the weakened Water channel.
• Water remains legal and can still be correct when raw matchup advantage is large enough; it is reduced, not disabled.
• A temporary Rain or other legal replacement removes both Blood Sun modifiers for its duration.
7. Caelor, the Last Magistrate — Iron Decree

rows: Fetterpot Lv139; Regnacra Lv140; Sigilume Lv141; Destridon Lv142; Cerberrood Lv143; Aegishorn Lv144
Slots 3 and 6 use Hidden Abilities; all other slots follow the frozen Checklist 04 authored assignments.
Steel/Fighting structure, forced order and defensive pivots.

blocks.text: Field contract
• All Steel-type damaging moves deal ×1.5 damage.
• All Fighting-type damaging moves deal ×0.5 damage.
• Iron Decree does not add a hidden Defence or Special Defence bonus. Caelor’s bulk comes from the frozen roster, held roles, legal moves and AI.
• The field modifies move damage only; it does not rewrite the type chart.
Viable counterplay
• Fire, Ground, status and special pressure are natural alternatives to the suppressed Fighting channel.
• Fighting remains usable when the underlying type matchup is strong enough; it is never forbidden.
• A temporary field replacement removes the Steel boost and Fighting suppression together.
8. Asterion, Voice of Certainty — Twin Radiance

rows: Caproclaim Lv151; Vortamor Lv152; Oriflamme Lv153; Tattereign Lv154; Pandemne Lv155; Serapine Lv156
Slots 3 and 6 use Hidden Abilities; all other slots follow the frozen Checklist 04 authored assignments.
Fairy/Dark mirrored pressure that punishes the obvious Dark answer without removing counterplay.

blocks.text: Field contract
• All Fairy-type damaging moves deal ×1.5 damage.
• All Dark-type damaging moves deal ×0.5 damage.
• Twin Radiance has no extra binary-choice, command-lock or forced-target mechanic. Its pressure is entirely represented by the visible damage modifiers.
• The field is symmetric and does not secretly favour the Warden’s individual stats.
Viable counterplay
• Steel and Poison pressure attack Fairy-heavy structures without leaning on the suppressed Dark channel.
• Strong neutral coverage remains a valid line.
• Temporary field replacement restores ordinary Dark/Fairy damage relationships for its duration.
9. Mirra, the Kindly Shape — Mourning Rain

rows: Deltacroc Lv161; Galvaneel Lv162; Galleonid Lv163; Palimopus Lv164; Fetterpot Lv165; Liontide Lv166
Slots 3 and 6 use Hidden Abilities; all other slots follow the frozen Checklist 04 authored assignments.
Rain sustain, deceptive recovery and repeated pressure.

blocks.text: Field contract
• All Water-type damaging moves deal ×1.5 damage.
• All Fire-type damaging moves deal ×0.5 damage.
• Mourning Rain itself contains no healing multiplier, accuracy change or illusion rule. Recovery comes from legal moves, abilities, held roles and the separate Mirra boss script.
• The field is symmetric: player Water benefits and player Fire is suppressed while active.
Viable counterplay
• Electric and Grass offence are obvious starting counters, while the frozen Water/Grass sustain structure is allowed to cover them.
• Anti-sustain status, pressure and strong neutral damage can win without using a single prescribed counter type.
• A temporary Sun or other legal replacement turns off Mourning Rain for its duration.
Boss-specific note
• Mirra’s deceptive duplicates/healing illusions are separate authored boss scripting, not part of Mourning Rain’s field rules.

• That script may create false visual copies or healing deception, but the real mechanical target must remain determinable through clear authored cues; core commands, move text and accessibility information stay readable.
• Exact event trigger/presentation belongs to story-event and battle-presentation implementation. It may not add an unlisted hidden field multiplier.
10. Velcar, the Oath-Eater — Cocytus Hail

rows: Grudgemont Lv171; Laureveil Lv172; Rimehart Lv173; Paleursa Lv174; Aegishorn Lv175; Tattereign Lv176
Slots 3 and 6 use Hidden Abilities; all other slots follow the frozen Checklist 04 authored assignments.
Ice attrition and punishment for predictable commitments.

blocks.text: Field contract
• At the normal end-of-turn field-damage step, every non-Ice active Abyssal loses 1/16 of maximum HP.
• Ice Abyssals are immune to Cocytus Hail chip damage.
• While Cocytus Hail is active, Ice Abyssals receive a ×1.5 Defence effective-stat modifier.
• The ×1.5 Ice Defence modifier is a field modifier, not a visible stat stage. It applies equally to player and enemy Ice Abyssals and disappears immediately while the field is suppressed.

• Cocytus Hail intentionally combines classic Hail chip with the modern Snow-style Ice Defence reward; it does not add other automatic Hail/Snow effects unless separately defined in the move/ability catalogue.
Viable counterplay
• Ice party members avoid chip and gain the same Defence bonus as the Warden’s Ice types.
• Fire, Fighting, Rock and Steel offence are natural pressure families where the actual species matchup supports them.
• A legal temporary field replacement suspends both Hail chip and the Ice Defence bonus.
11. Nema, the Unremembered — Quiet Night

rows: Vesperyre Lv179; Carriena Lv180; Galleonid Lv181; Murmite Lv182; Pandemne Lv183; Noctafey Lv184
Slots 3 and 6 use Hidden Abilities; all other slots follow the frozen Checklist 04 authored assignments.
Dark/Ghost suppression, silence and late-game switching pressure.

blocks.text: Field contract
• All Dark-type damaging moves deal ×1.5 damage.
• All Fairy-type damaging moves deal ×0.5 damage.
• Quiet Night does not hide, rename or disable commands, move labels, target indicators, status icons or accessibility tooltips.
• Atmospheric loss of names may affect decorative world/battle presentation, but never the semantic information required to make a legal battle decision.
Viable counterplay
• Fighting, Bug and strong neutral pressure avoid overreliance on the weakened Fairy channel.
• Fairy is suppressed rather than prohibited and can remain correct when type advantage is large enough.
• Temporary field replacement turns off both Quiet Night modifiers for its duration.
12. Field replacement and resumption state machine

rows: Native field is active and announced before Turn 1.
Native field becomes dormant; none of its damage, chip or defensive modifiers apply.
Normal replacement semantics apply. The discarded temporary field does not resume later.
Native field automatically returns at once with indefinite duration.
Clearing does not create permanent neutrality; native field immediately reasserts.
Attempt to clear native field without replacement
Native field remains. It cannot be permanently dispelled during its Warden battle.
Victory resolution wins priority; no extra native-field chip tick is added after the battle is already won.

NO UNDERLAY STACKING
A dormant Warden field contributes nothing while a temporary replacement is active. This includes Ossael’s Rock Special Defence bonus and Velcar’s Ice Defence bonus. The moment the native field resumes, all of its listed rules resume together.

blocks.text: 13. Damage, chip and defensive-modifier semantics
• Type-damage fields modify the damage of the move’s resolved attacking type. They do not alter the attacker’s type, defender’s type or the effectiveness chart.
• Ordinary type effectiveness is resolved first as a logical matchup. A true immunity remains 0 damage; multiplying 0 by a field bonus never breaks an immunity.

• Field multipliers are dedicated multiplicative damage modifiers inside the canonical battle-damage pipeline. Exact integer rounding remains governed by the project’s core battle-math implementation, not redefined separately per Warden.
• Gilded Dust and Cocytus Hail chip uses 1/16 maximum HP at the normal field-damage step and affects both sides under the same eligibility rule.

• Rock Special Defence ×1.5 and Ice Defence ×1.5 are effective-stat field modifiers rather than +1/+2 stat stages. They therefore do not consume a stage, display as a stage, or get removed by a generic stat-stage reset. They end only when their field is not active.
• Field defensive modifiers combine with ordinary stat stages, abilities, items and other legal battle modifiers through the normal battle-math system; there is no Warden-only stacking exception.
14. HUD, readability and accessibility
• A persistent field indicator is visible throughout every Warden battle. It shows the active field name and an icon distinct from status-condition icons.
• Inspecting/holding the indicator displays the exact mechanical text in plain language, including numeric multipliers, chip fraction, immunities and any defensive field bonus.

• When a temporary replacement is active, the HUD shows that field as ACTIVE and the native Warden field as DORMANT / RETURNS AFTER REPLACEMENT. If the replacement has a turn countdown, the remaining turns are shown.
• Opening field text is concise and mechanical. The player never has to remember pre-battle dialogue to know what the field does.
• Nema may distort decorative labels or world presentation for theme, but battle commands and semantic move information remain readable. Veyr likewise cannot obscure core target or move data.
• Colour is never the only carrier of field state. Name, icon and text are all available.
15. Implementation data contract

Recommended stable data fields below are implementation identifiers, not additional game mechanics. They exist so the battle engine can represent every Warden field with the same generic field system.
• Every Warden battle references one nativeFieldId and sets nativeFieldPersistent=true.
• Runtime state tracks activeFieldId separately from nativeFieldId so temporary replacement never destroys the native reference.
• When activeFieldId is cleared/expired and the battle owner is a Warden with an undefeated battle state, activeFieldId resets to nativeFieldId.
• UI text must be generated from the same numeric data used by battle calculation so the displayed rule cannot drift from the implemented rule.

FINAL STATUS
CHECKLIST 05 — HELL TERRAIN FINALISATION: COMPLETE / LOCKED. Later implementation may bind event IDs, VFX, move IDs and generic battle-order details, but must not silently alter the eight native field payloads, symmetry rules, persistence, replacement/resumption behaviour or readable-UI contract in this specification.
